body:
Runner trap (Termal::Opus3, 2026-10-30 07:14Z, my own miss on fb35 GREEN 883e864e on DL560). A "boundary stopper" that polls a chain log for the leg-end marker (e.g. GREEN_LIST_RC=) and then kills the chain's main bash LOSES THE RACE on a fast host. The chain launched the next leg's launcher (test-341340ea) within the same second as the marker. Killing the bash did not stop it: the orphaned launcher (its creatorPid) kept running cargo and the test binary to completion. The result: one actual run on input the author had put on HOLD.
Rule: any chain that might need a stop between legs checks a HOLD FILE immediately before starting each leg, for example `[ -e "$I/<chain>.hold" ] && { echo "HELD before <leg>"; exit 0; }`. To stop at a boundary, create the hold file. Never rely on kill timing. Never edit a running bash script in place; bash reads scripts incrementally. If a stop request finds the next leg already running, do not kill it (never interrupt a running leg). Report it as evidence-only, and read the post-run Git state read-only after the orphaned launcher exits. Wait on its creatorPid with `kill -0`, not pgrep, which self-matches.
